title: Add Momentum Mode to Capture Trending Regime Profits Being Left on Table
analysis: On 2026-05-22, the bot attempted 5 consecutive AAPL BUY entries with signals 'RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25 (trending)' — all correctly rejected by duplicate-position logic, but all carrying a 2.0 R:R and HIGH/MEDIUM confidence. On 2026-05-25, the bot identified AAPL (RSI=80.46, ADX=38.14) and AMD (RSI=73.15, ADX=57.97) as best candidates with momentum scores of 4, yet was forced to skip because the system has no momentum execution pathway. The QQQ trade on 2026-05-22 (signals: RSI>65, AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25, 20DayHighBreakout, score=5) was SUBMITTED — confirming the signal detection engine already produces valid momentum setups. Current macro supports this: SPY is 1.93% above its 20-day MA (745.64 vs 731.58), Technology sector is up +3.46% over 5 days, VIX at 16.59 (low-vol, risk-on). The ADX>30 hard rule (Rule 6) correctly blocks mean reversion entries in trending regimes, but leaves the bot with zero actionable trades during sustained trending periods — which is exactly the regime the market is currently in.
rationale: The strategy is systematically blind to an entire market regime. When ADX>30 fires, the bot goes dark rather than pivoting to trend-following entries. The signal detection logic already identifies these setups (AAPL, AMD, QQQ momentum scores of 4-5), the R:R is confirmed viable (2.0:1), and the macro regime is aligned. Adding a gated momentum mode — activated only when ADX>30 AND price above MA20 AND RSI>60 — transforms rejected cycles into revenue cycles without touching the mean reversion logic.

insight.why_now: The market is in a confirmed trending regime (SPY above MA20 by 1.93%, Technology +3.46% in 5 days, AAPL ADX=38.14, AMD ADX=57.97). The bot has been generating HIGH-confidence momentum signals for days but has no execution pathway for them. This is not a signal failure — it is a strategy coverage gap.
insight.purpose: Capture the trending regime profits that the mean reversion system structurally cannot access, using a separate momentum entry ruleset gated behind strict regime conditions.
insight.expected_effect: Converts near-zero-trade days (May 25: 13+ consecutive skips despite 4 HIGH-confidence signals) into active trading days. Based on QQQ entry on May 22 (submitted, 2.0 R:R, score=5), momentum trades in this regime carry equivalent or superior R:R to mean reversion setups.
insight.risks: Momentum entries in late-stage trends risk buying the top. Late-cycle momentum trades (RSI>80) carry higher reversal risk. Must enforce strict ADX minimum, recency of breakout, and reduced position sizing (1% risk vs 1.5%) for momentum mode to avoid overexposure at trend exhaustion.

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. MOMENTUM MODE EXCEPTION: If ADX > 30 AND price is above MA20 by >1% AND RSI > 60 AND a 20-day high breakout is confirmed on above-average volume, a momentum entry is permitted with the following constraints: (a) risk per trade reduced to 1.0% of account, (b) stop loss set at 1x ATR below entry, (c) take profit at 2x ATR above entry, (d) maximum 2 simultaneous momentum positions, (e) no momentum entries after 14:30 EST.

title: Signal Contamination: Bot Is Generating Momentum Signals Inside Mean Reversion Scorer
analysis: On 2026-05-22, five AAPL entries fired signals 'RSI>65 (strong momentum), AboveMA20>1%, ADX>25 (trending)' with signal_score=4. These are anti-signals for mean reversion — RSI>65 is overbought, not oversold. Yet the scoring engine assigned score=4, meeting the 2+ threshold required for entry. The SIGNAL SCORING section in CLAUDE.md only defines RSI<35 (+2), RSI<45 (+1), BelowBB (+1), BelowMA20>1% (+1), ADX<25 (+1) — all mean reversion signals. There is no defined rule for how RSI>65 or AboveMA20 generates a score of 4. This means the bot is operating a shadow scoring system for momentum signals that is not documented in CLAUDE.md, has no defined minimum threshold specific to momentum, and is routing those scores through the mean reversion entry gate. The only reason these didn't execute was the duplicate-position block on AAPL — not because the risk rules correctly filtered them. The QQQ momentum trade on 2026-05-22 DID execute (score=5, SUBMITTED) under these undocumented rules.
rationale: Undocumented scoring pathways are a systemic risk. The QQQ trade on May 22 executed under momentum signals using the mean reversion R:R gate and position sizing. If that trade had been a loss, it would have been attributable to a strategy the system was never designed to run. CLAUDE.md must explicitly define the momentum signal scoring rubric, its entry conditions, and its separation from mean reversion sizing rules — or momentum scoring must be disabled until the momentum mode is formally sanctioned (see suggestion 1).

insight.why_now: The QQQ SUBMITTED trade on 2026-05-22 is direct evidence that momentum trades are already executing live under undocumented rules. This is not a future risk — it is a current operational gap. With 4 open positions already held and account at ~$99k, an undocumented execution pathway is a capital protection failure.
insight.purpose: Enforce auditability and intentionality. Every executed trade must be traceable to an explicit rule in CLAUDE.md. Undocumented scoring means the weekly review cannot correctly attribute wins/losses to strategy logic.
insight.expected_effect: Closes the gap between what CLAUDE.md says the bot does and what it actually does. Prevents accidental momentum execution under mean reversion position sizing during unfavorable conditions (e.g., late-trend entries with RSI>80).
insight.risks: Disabling momentum scoring entirely while the regime is trending (ADX>30) would return the bot to the zero-trade condition seen on May 25. The correct path is to document and gate momentum scoring formally, not eliminate it.

current_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING (need 2+ to enter under medium_safety profile)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)
proposed_rule:
## SIGNAL SCORING — MEAN REVERSION MODE (need 2+ to enter; active when ADX < 30)
- RSI < 35: +2 points (strong oversold)
- RSI < 45: +1 point (mild oversold)
- Price below lower Bollinger Band: +1 point
- Price below MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX < 25 (ranging market): +1 point (regime confirmation)

## SIGNAL SCORING — MOMENTUM MODE (need 4+ to enter; active ONLY when ADX > 30 per Rule 6 momentum exception)
- RSI > 65: +2 points (strong momentum)
- RSI > 55: +1 point (mild momentum)
- Price above MA20 by > 1%: +1 point
- ADX > 30 (trending market): +1 point (regime confirmation)
- 20-day high breakout confirmed on above-average volume: +1 point
NOTE: Momentum signals MUST NOT be evaluated when ADX < 30. Mean reversion signals MUST NOT be evaluated when ADX > 30. Scores from the two modes are never combined.

title: BTC/USDT Is Generating Null Signal Data — Remove or Fix Crypto Data Pipeline
analysis: From 2026-05-25T16:09 through 18:18 (10 consecutive cycles), every skip entry shows 'Best candidate: BTC/USDT mode=NONE score=0 (needs 2+) MR=0 Mom=0 RSI=? ADX=? regime=?'. All technical indicators are returning '?' — not zero, not a valid value, but a missing data sentinel. This means the Binance/CCXT integration is failing to return usable RSI, ADX, or regime data for BTC/USDT. During these 10 cycles, the bot is consuming compute cycles, logging entries, and potentially blocking evaluation of other instruments (it reports 4 open positions throughout May 25 with zero P&L change — suggesting a possible position accounting freeze as well). The account value is frozen at exactly $99,062.18 from 2026-05-24T09:48 through 2026-05-25T18:18 — 33+ hours with zero P&L movement and 4 reported open positions. This suggests either the position data is stale/frozen or all 4 open positions have been closed and the portfolio is in cash but the open_positions counter is not updating.
rationale: A data pipeline returning '?' for all indicators is a silent failure mode. The bot is not erroring out — it is silently evaluating broken data and producing structured skip entries that look normal in the log. The frozen account value ($99,062.18 for 33+ hours across a trading day) and static open_positions=4 with zero P&L delta is a strong indicator of a state management bug, potentially triggered by the crypto data failure. BTC/USDT mean reversion suitability is also questionable: crypto exhibits higher volatility regimes, lower mean reversion reliability, and the current Binance/CCXT integration appears unreliable. Until the data pipeline is verified, BTC/USDT should be suspended from the watchlist.

insight.why_now: The null data pattern begins at 16:09 on May 25 and persists through the last journal entry at 18:18 — representing the most recent operational state of the system. This is an active failure, not a historical one. The account value freeze coincides exactly with the crypto data failure onset.
insight.purpose: Restore data integrity and eliminate false-negative skip cycles caused by broken indicator feeds. Prevent state freeze from propagating into the next trading session.
insight.expected_effect: Eliminating broken BTC/USDT cycles restores the bot's ability to correctly identify and act on the best available equity candidate during each cycle. Resolving the position state freeze ensures P&L tracking and open_positions limits are accurate.
insight.risks: If BTC/USDT is removed and the underlying cause is a broker connectivity issue affecting equities too, the fix may mask a broader data problem. The position freeze should be investigated independently of the watchlist change.

proposed_rule:
## WATCHLIST HEALTH CHECK (enforced at session start)
Before evaluating any symbol, verify that RSI, ADX, and regime data return numeric values (not null, '?', or zero for all three simultaneously). If a symbol returns invalid indicator data for 3 consecutive cycles, it must be flagged as DATA_FAILURE and excluded from evaluation for the remainder of the session. Log the failure with timestamp. BTC/USDT is suspended from the active watchlist pending Binance/CCXT data pipeline verification. Crypto instruments may only be re-added after a validated 5-day backtest confirms indicator data integrity.

title: Add Momentum/Trend-Following Sleeve to Capture Dominant Regime
analysis: Across all 50 journal entries, the system generated ZERO executed trades despite detecting high-confidence momentum signals repeatedly. On 2026-05-25 and 2026-05-26, the best candidates logged were AAPL (RSI=80.46–81.45, ADX=38.14–42.34, momentum score=4) and AMD (RSI=73.15–77.93, ADX=56.71–57.97, momentum score=5) — both flagged as TRENDING and correctly rejected by the mean reversion filter. The account sat at ~$99,062–$100,108 for the entire observation window with open_positions locked at 4–5 (existing holds), generating no new alpha. The macro context confirms this is not a mean reversion environment: SPY is 2.35% above its 20-day MA (750.59 vs 733.36), Technology sector is up +6.87% over 5 days, and VIX is 17.01 — elevated enough to suppress deep oversold dislocations but not high enough to warrant sitting out entirely. The system correctly identifies trending instruments but has no strategy module to act on them, leaving a structural alpha gap every session.
rationale: A pure mean reversion system is regime-dependent by design. In a trending regime (ADX>30 on leading names, SPY above MA20, Tech +6.87% in 5 days), mean reversion signals will be structurally absent for the dominant instruments. Adding a momentum sleeve — activated only when ADX>30 and RSI>65 on a 20-day high breakout — allows the system to harvest returns from the regime it is actually in, rather than waiting for a regime it is not in. This is not strategy dilution; it is regime-adaptive capital deployment. The two modules are complementary: mean reversion fires in ranging markets, momentum fires in trending markets, and the ADX threshold (already in Rule 6) gates which module is active.

insight.why_now: On 2026-05-25 and 2026-05-26 alone, AMD scored momentum=5 with ADX=56–57 and AAPL scored momentum=4 with ADX=42 across 15+ consecutive cycles. These are textbook trend-following setups the system saw, logged with HIGH confidence, and was structurally forbidden from trading. The opportunity cost is not theoretical — it is documented in the journal.
insight.purpose: Unlock a second strategy module that activates in the trending regime the current watchlist is already exhibiting, converting detected-but-skipped HIGH-confidence signals into executable trades.
insight.expected_effect: In trending regimes (ADX>30, SPY>MA20, sector momentum positive), the momentum sleeve should generate 2–5 new trade entries per week on the existing watchlist. At the observed R:R of 2.0:1 (as seen in the AMD BUY on 2026-05-26 at entry 495.78, stop 470.52, target 546.30) and 1.5% risk per trade, each executed trade targets ~$2,250 gain on a ~$100K account. Even a 45% win rate at 2:1 R:R produces positive expectancy (EV = 0.45×2 − 0.55×1 = +0.35R per trade).
insight.risks: Momentum strategies are vulnerable to sharp reversals; a late-cycle entry on AAPL at RSI=81 carries mean-reversion risk from the opposing module's own signals. Requires strict position independence — a momentum long on AMD must not coexist with a mean reversion long on AMD. Also risks regime misclassification during transitions (ADX crossing 30 threshold).

current_rule: 6. TREND FILTER: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals.
proposed_rule: 6. TREND FILTER & REGIME ROUTING: If ADX > 30, regime is TRENDING — do NOT take mean reversion signals. Instead, route to MOMENTUM MODULE: entry permitted if (a) RSI > 65, (b) price above MA20 by >1%, (c) 20-day high breakout confirmed on above-average volume, (d) ADX > 30, and (e) R:R ≥ 1.5:1 with stop at 0.75x ATR below entry. Momentum entries use identical position sizing (1.5% risk) and are subject to all hard rules. A symbol may not simultaneously hold a mean reversion position and a momentum position.

title: Remove BTC/USDT From Active Scanning Until Data Feed Is Operational
analysis: From 2026-05-25 16:09 through 2026-05-26 18:39, BTC/USDT appeared as the best candidate in 18 consecutive SKIP entries — every single one logging 'RSI=? ADX=? regime=?' indicating a completely non-functional data feed. The system cycled through these BTC/USDT evaluations at high frequency (sometimes every 10–20 minutes) consuming decision cycles, generating log noise, and surfacing as 'best candidate' purely because equity candidates had already been evaluated and were at max positions. This is not a low-signal environment — it is a broken data environment being mistaken for one. During this same window, the account_value remained completely flat at $99,062.18 across all 29 BTC/USDT-dominated entries, confirming zero productive activity.
rationale: A candidate with RSI=?, ADX=?, regime=? should score 0 and should never surface as 'best candidate.' Its repeated appearance as best candidate indicates the equity scanner is either exhausted (all positions full or no signals) or the candidate ranking logic does not penalise missing data. Keeping a broken instrument in the active universe wastes compute cycles, pollutes the journal with non-informative entries, and creates false impression of market scanning activity. Either fix the Binance/CCXT feed or gate BTC/USDT behind a data-quality check that requires all required fields to be non-null before the symbol enters candidate ranking.

insight.why_now: 18 of the 50 journal entries (36%) are dominated by BTC/USDT with completely null indicator data. This is an active data quality failure occurring in real-time, not a historical artifact.
insight.purpose: Eliminate null-data candidates from surfacing in best-candidate logs, reduce journal noise, and ensure the system's scan output reflects only evaluable instruments.
insight.expected_effect: Cleaner journal entries, accurate identification of true scan results, and prevention of the system appearing to scan while producing no actionable output. Secondary effect: if BTC feed is fixed, crypto universe adds genuine mean reversion candidates with 24/7 trading hours that complement equity session gaps.
insight.risks: If BTC/USDT is removed entirely and the feed issue is transient, the system loses a diversifying asset class. Recommended approach is a data-quality gate (not removal) so the symbol re-enters candidate evaluation automatically when feed is restored.

proposed_rule: DATA QUALITY GATE (new rule 12): Before any symbol enters candidate ranking, all required indicator fields (RSI, ADX, ATR, price vs MA20, Bollinger Band position) must return non-null values. Any symbol with one or more null indicator fields is assigned score=0 and tagged 'DATA_UNAVAILABLE' — it must NOT appear in best_candidate logs and must NOT consume a decision cycle. Log the data failure separately in a system_health log. This gate applies to all assets including crypto.

title: Implement Opportunity Cost Logging to Quantify Regime Mismatch in Real-Time
analysis: The system correctly skipped all trending signals per its rules, but there is no mechanism to quantify what those skips cost in forgone P&L. AMD was detected at entry 495.78 with R:R=2.0 on 2026-05-26; by the same session the account was up only $1,029 (1.03% day gain) from existing positions. Meanwhile AMD's momentum score of 5 with ADX=56.88 represents a near-ideal trend entry. AAPL with RSI=81.39 and ADX=42.34 was similarly skipped 8+ times on 2026-05-26. The system has no way to flag to its operators: 'This regime has been TRENDING for N consecutive sessions; mean reversion signal frequency has dropped X%; estimated forgone momentum P&L is $Y.' Without this signal, the operator cannot make an informed decision about when to activate an alternative module or expand the universe to include range-bound instruments better suited to current conditions.
rationale: Regime mismatch is the single largest structural risk to a single-strategy system. The journal data shows the system has been in a near-zero new-entry state for at least 5 consecutive trading days (May 22–26) while holding the same 4–5 positions. This is a regime lock-out, not disciplined patience. A real-time regime health metric — tracking the ratio of TRENDING skips to total evaluations, consecutive days without a new mean reversion entry, and the cumulative momentum signal score of skipped candidates — would allow the operator to make evidence-based decisions about strategy routing rather than discovering the regime mismatch only in weekly review.

insight.why_now: 50 entries, 0 new executed trades, 4–5 positions unchanged throughout. The system has been regime-locked for the entire observable window. This is only visible in retrospect by counting journal entries; it is not surfaced as an operational alert.
insight.purpose: Surface regime mismatch as a real-time operational signal so that strategy routing decisions (activating momentum module, expanding watchlist to range-bound ETFs, or reducing scan frequency) can be made proactively.
insight.expected_effect: Faster operator response to regime transitions, reduced opportunity cost from prolonged single-regime lock-out, and a documented basis for strategy configuration changes that is grounded in observed signal data rather than intuition.
insight.risks: Overly sensitive regime alerts could prompt premature strategy switching. The metric should require a minimum threshold (e.g., 3 consecutive trading days with <1 mean reversion entry AND >50% of best-candidate slots occupied by TRENDING skips) before triggering an alert, to avoid noise during normal slow-signal periods.

proposed_rule:
## WEEKLY REVIEW PROMPT
When given a batch of journal entries, identify:
- Win rate and average R-multiple

- REGIME HEALTH REPORT: (a) Ratio of TRENDING-regime skips to total evaluations over the review period; (b) Consecutive trading days with zero new mean reversion entries; (c) Sum of momentum signal scores from all TRENDING skips (proxy for forgone momentum P&L); (d) Regime classification for each day (TRENDING/RANGING/VOLATILE/LOW-VOL) based on ADX and VIX; (e) Flag if system has been regime-locked (no new entries for 3+ consecutive days) and identify which alternative strategy module would have been applicable.
